record.paper_title: SYMMETRY AND COLORINGS: SOME RESULTS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: Classify ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in Rⁿ when n > 2. In particular, determine ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in Rⁿ with n > 2, and compute ms(T, 2) for the regular tetrahedron T in R³, equivalently ms(S₄ × I, 2).

evidence.quote: For every finite r we define ms(X, r) to be the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that for every measurable r-coloring of X there exists a monochromatic subset A ⊂ X of measure µ(A) ≥ ε such that A = g · A for some non-identity element g ∈ G.

7.4. Problem. Classify ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in Rn, where n > 2. In particular, calculate ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in Rn for n > 2. Calculate ms(T, 2) (or equivalently, ms(S4 × I, 2)) for the regular tetrahedron T in R3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group acting on a set $X$. For a subset $A \subseteq X$, say that $A$ is symmetric (with respect to the action) if there exists a non-identity element $g \in G$ such that $gA = A$.

Now let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a compact set of positive Lebesgue measure, and let $G$ be its isometry group (the group of Euclidean isometries of $\mathbb{R}^n$ that map $X$ onto itself), acting on $X$. Let $\mu$ denote Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. For an integer $r \geq 2$, a measurable $r$-coloring of $X$ is a partition $X = C_1 \cup \cdots \cup C_r$ into $r$ Lebesgue-measurable subsets.

Define
$$ \mathrm{ms}(X, r) \;=\; \sup\{\varepsilon \geq 0 : \text{for every measurable } r\text{-coloring of } X \text{ there exists a monochromatic} $$
$$ \text{symmetric subset } A \subseteq C_i \text{ with } \mu(A) \geq \varepsilon\}, $$
where "monochromatic symmetric" means $A$ is contained in a single color class $C_i$ and $gA = A$ for some non-identity $g \in G$.

Problems:
(a) Classify (i.e., give a method to compute) $\mathrm{ms}(X, r)$ for arbitrary compact subsets $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ of positive Lebesgue measure, when $n > 2$.

(b) In particular, compute $\mathrm{ms}(X, r)$ for every regular polyhedron $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n > 2$, for all integers $r \geq 2$.

(c) Compute $\mathrm{ms}(T, 2)$, where $T$ is the regular tetrahedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (equivalently, compute $\mathrm{ms}(S_4 \times I, 2)$ where the symmetric group $S_4$ acts on the tetrahedron's symmetry structure and $I$ denotes the standard interval factor in this reformulation).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the foundational treatment of $\mathrm{ms}(X,r)$ by Banakh, Verbitsky, and Vorobets ("A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry," Electron. J. Combin.) and a later note on the Lobachevsky-plane analogue, but no source was found that classifies $\mathrm{ms}(X,r)$ for compact sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n>2$, computes the value for general regular polyhedra in higher dimensions, or determines $\mathrm{ms}(T,2)$ for the regular tetrahedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The status appears to remain unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper introducing ms(Ω, r) for measurable colorings and monochromatic symmetric subsets.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework but does not resolve the higher-dimensional classification or the tetrahedron case.

status_evidence.title: Symmetric monochromatic subsets in colorings of the Lobachevsky plane
status_evidence.snippet: Studies analogous ms-type quantities in hyperbolic geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Related work, not addressing the Euclidean higher-dimensional polyhedra problem.
